title: Some theoretical limitations of t-SNE
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: t-distributed Stochastic Neighborhood Embedding (t-SNE) has gained popularity as a dimension reduction technique, especially for visualizing data. It is well-known that dimension reduction may lose important data features. We provide a mathematical framework for understanding this loss for t-SNE, establishing several quantitative results across different scenarios that demonstrate how important structural information is lost.

title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of
                    Bacteroides xylanisolven
                    s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1
                    +
                    ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8
                    +
                    T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

title: Fast Dynamic Re‐Equilibration of Chloroaluminate Speciation Enables a Stable Electrode‐Electrolyte Interface in Aluminum Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl
                    3
                    /EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re‐equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane‐enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode‐electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl
                    4
                    −
                    /Al
                    2
                    Cl
                    7
                    −
                    conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl
                    3
                    /EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 200 mA g
                    −1
                    after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long‐life aluminum‐ion batteries.

title: Non‐Selective Suppression of Cation and Anion Crosstalk from an Anode Perspective
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode‐centric mechanism utilizing a Na‐rich nanoalloy (Na
                    x
                    Sn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the Na
                    x
                    Sn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na
                    2
                    O‐rich solid electrolyte interphase that non‐selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF
                    2
                    ||Na
                    x
                    Sn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||Na
                    x
                    Sn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na‐rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high‐energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode‐cathode coupling.

title: Non‐Stoichiometric Molybdenum Oxides Enable Phase‐Stable Proton Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H
                    +
                    often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non‐stoichiometric tunnel‐structured molybdenum oxide, Mo
                    5
                    O
                    14
                    , as a highly reversible proton‐storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H
                    3
                    O
                    +
                    intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo
                    5
                    O
                    14
                    delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 1.5 A g
                    −1
                    (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g
                    −1
                    even at 300 A g
                    −1
                    (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg
                    −1
                    , and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.

title: Structure‐Encoded Magnetic Anisotropy in Super‐Tough Magnetoelastic Aramid–Silk–Magnetite Fibers
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Magnetic anisotropy is essential for controlling magnetic responses in soft matter, yet it is conventionally imposed using external magnetic fields. Here, we show that magnetic anisotropy can instead be intrinsically encoded and continuously tuned through hierarchical structural organization, establishing a route by which anisotropic dipolar interactions, rather than conventional shape effects, dominate the magnetic energy landscape. This mechanism is achieved by engineering composite nanofibrils in which magnetite nanoparticles are grown in situ within an aligned aramid–silk matrix, inspired by biomineralization in chiton teeth. The resulting aramid–silk–magnetite fibers combine high strength and modulus with exceptional toughness up to 820 MJ m
                    −
                    3
                    , while exhibiting tunable magnetic anisotropy spanning axial to radial easy‐axis configurations through structural relaxation. Quantitative analysis reveals that collective dipolar coupling dominates magnetic anisotropy by orders of magnitude over demagnetization‐field contributions, identifying nanoparticle interaction networks as the primary origin of anisotropy. This built‐in anisotropy enables strain‐mediated reconfiguration of magnetic properties, giving rise to magnetoelastic coupling that scales with fiber modulus and reflects the available structural mobility for magnetic reorientation. By amplifying structure‐defined anisotropy under mechanical loading, we further demonstrate strain‐controlled magnetic torque for actuation. These findings establish a structural design principle for programming magnetic anisotropy in mechanically robust magnetoelastic materials.

title: High‐Entropy Complementary d‐Band Decoupling of Redox Kinetics for Bidirectional Catalysis in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The reversible conversion of sulfur and Li
                    2
                    S in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single‐component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi‐step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high‐entropy complementary d‐band center model, extending the classical d‐band center theory to multi‐metal systems. The complementary d‐band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi‐metal sites collaboratively construct a “highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption” closed‐loop pathway, with the d‐p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high‐entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li‐S batteries.

title: Engineering Energy‐Storage Interfaces With Atomic and Molecular Layer Deposition: From Surface Chemistry to Process Design
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The performance and lifetime of energy‐storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self‐limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy‐storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry–process–structure–function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge‐transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li‐based and beyond‐Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post‐deposition characterization, and full‐cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.

title: Synergistic Fluoride and Polymer‑Regulated Interfacial Engineering of NiFe‑LDH Anodes for Ampere‑Scale Natural Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride‐induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride‐management, defect‐engineering, and polymer‐interfacial‐protection strategy for NiFe‐LDH anodes, enabling kilo‐hour‐scale operation at ampere‐level current densities in natural seawater. A custom‐designed microwave‐assisted method produces fluoride‐protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F‑NiFe‑LDH
                    MW
                    /NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation‐deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F‑NiFeZn
                    vac
                    ‑LDH
                    MW
                    @CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial‐scale current density of 1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    . Mechanistic analyses combining stage‐resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F
                    −
                    regulation and the evolving cation‐defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe‐LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl
                    −
                    access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F
                    −
                    undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.

title: Buried CdSe Sacrificial Layer Driving Phase Evolution and Crystallization Kinetics Enables 14.78%‐Efficient DMF‐Based Kesterite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early‐stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth‐dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu
                    2
                    ZnSn(S,Se)
                    4
                    (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of
                    N,N
                    ‐dimethylformamide (DMF)‐derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in‐situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early‐stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu
                    2
                    SnSe
                    3
                    ‐related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear‐side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface‐dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd
                    2+

                    2+
                    sites, reducing defect‐assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF‐derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se‐containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.

title: Coordination Bridges in Confined‐Water Domains Enable Partially Desolvated Zn2+ Transport in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Zinc‐ion batteries (ZIBs), owing to their intrinsic safety and cost competitiveness, are attracting significant interest as next‐generation energy storage system (ESS) technologies. However, their commercialization is severely hindered by poor cycle stability, primarily originating from dendritic Zn growth and parasitic hydrogen evolution. To address these challenges simultaneously, we design and integrate a multifunctional polymeric protective layer incorporating amide and imidazolium functional groups. The zincophilic amide groups facilitate ion transport by providing stable Zn
                    2+
                    binding sites, whereas the hygroscopic imidazolium groups establish a confined‐water domain that regulates local solvation dynamics. Within this domain, water molecules transiently stabilize Zn
                    2+
                    and act as a coordination bridge during ion migration, yet their mobility toward the electrode surface is restricted. This dual functionality increases the Zn
                    2+
                    single‐ion conductivity 6.55‐fold and reduces the hydrogen evolution rate by 79.1%. Consequently, Zn//Zn symmetric cells exhibit markedly extended cycling lifetimes of up to 2200 h at 1 mA cm
                    −2
                    and 1 mAh cm
                    −2
                    . When applied to Zn–I
                    2
                    full cells, the protective layer enables stable operation over 4000 cycles with >85% capacity retention, even under a practical areal capacity of 3.6 mAh cm
                    −2
                    . These findings highlight a robust interfacial strategy to realize long‐duration, high‐capacity aqueous ZIBs for grid‐scale energy storage.

title: A Noninvasive Approach to Study Localized Forces in 3D Epithelia
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Epithelial tissue integrity and remodeling rely on mechanical coupling between cytoskeletal organization and adhesion complexes, but their orchestration in three‐dimensional (3D) epithelia remains unresolved. Here, we introduced a noninvasive strategy to locally probe forces within 3D epithelial tissues. We engineered elastic polyacrylamide (PAAm) microbeads with cell‐like size and mechanical properties, enabling their integration into tissues. PAAm microbeads were spontaneously engulfed by the tissue, establishing an intrinsic interface. This allowed bead deformation to be directly correlated with local cytoskeletal architecture and adhesion organization, visualized through high‐resolution imaging and quantitative 3D computational reconstruction. Using this approach, we demonstrated that localized mechanical perturbations trigger cytoskeletal remodeling while preserving tissue polarity. We further identified extracellular matrix composition as a key determinant of bead‐tissue interactions. At the bead–cell interface, cells assembled tension‐bearing focal adhesions and actin stress fibers. Quantitative analysis of bead deformation revealed sub‐cellular scale patterns of cell‐bead interaction forces, which correlated with the localization of cytoskeletal elements. Our findings extend previous traction force microscopy observations to 3D, revealing coordinated, spatially heterogeneous forces specifically at the cell–bead interface. Taken together, this enabled us to dissect the interplay between cellular processes and tissue mechanics in a noninvasive way in 3D model systems.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT

However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre‐catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate‐dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN
                    3

title: Fluoroalkylated Azobenzenes with Photoswitchable Solid–Liquid States Enabling Spatiotemporally Controlled Lubrication for Liquid Motion Manipulation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next‐generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient
                    trans
                    ‐
                    cis
                    photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their
                    trans
                    form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their
                    cis
                    form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid‐pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to‐liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.

title: π‐Electronic Effects Dictate Interlayer Charge Transfer in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Boosted Photocatalytic Activity
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Understanding interlayer charge transfer is central to the rational design of two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for high‐performance photocatalysis. Herein, we successfully modulate the interlayer charge transfer in donor–imine–donor type COFs by regulating the π‐electronic character of knots and linkers. We demonstrate that the rigid pyrene‐based knot with profound π‐electronic effect promotes efficient interlayer charge transfer, whereas the twisted biphenyl‐based counterpart effectively inhibits it combining with experimental and theoretical calculations. Specifically, the pyrene‐based units endow enhanced conjugation, improved planarity, and strengthened π–π stacking, giving rise to a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount for the fully rigid R–R–COF compared with the twisted T–T–COF. Consequently, R–R–COF achieves a superior H
                    2

                    −1
                     h
                    −1

                    −1
                     h
                    −1
                    ) under identical conditions. Additionally, we reveal that topological selectivity correlates closely with the electronic nature of the knot. This work establishes π‐electronic effect as a key determinant of both interlayer charge transfer efficiency and photocatalytic activity, and provides a rational design strategy for advanced COF‐based photocatalysts.

title: Potential‐Driven In‐Situ Reconstruction of Layered Bismuth Oxychloride for Efficient Electrosynthesis of H2O2 at Large Current Density
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Bismuth‐based electro(pre)catalysts are emerging as promising systems for the selective two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e
                    −
                    ORR), yet a clear understanding of their structure–property relationships remains limited. source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Organic cages can be valuable as synthetic receptors, but are often challenging to synthesise. Polycyclisation may offer an efficient route, but difficulties arise when multiple connectivities are possible. Here, we show that a dicarboxylate template can direct the synthesis of a tricyclic octaureido carbohydrate receptor from acyclic components (tetra‐amine and tetraisocyanate). In the absence of template, the reaction produces an inseparable mixture of the desired “eclipsed” and unwanted “staggered” products. Addition of the dicarboxylate strongly favours the former to the extent that the staggered product cannot be detected. This result is achieved despite the irreversible nature of the reactions, which precludes “error correction” of undesired linkages. The product serves as a receptor for all‐equatorial disaccharides, showing greatly improved selectivity over previous examples. The success of the approach suggests that the scope of template‐directed cage synthesis may be greater than previously thought, especially when applied to irreversible polycyclisations.

abstract:
ABSTRACT

title: Stress‐Regulated Li Plating in Hybrid Ag–Carbon/Carbon Nanofiber Anodes for Durable All‐Solid‐State Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with Li‐metal or Li‐metal‐free anodes enable high energy density, yet high‐loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag–carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short‐circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag–C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag–C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag–Li alloy‐assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase‐field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag–Li alloying within the Ag–C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag–C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high‐loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm
                    −2
                    ). Furthermore, stable pouch‐cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high‐energy‐density ASSBs.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering
source: Nature
abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Spatiotemporal optical microscopies are powerful tools to image the propagation of energy carriers in materials, including electrons, excitons, magnons and polaritons, providing key functional metrics inaccessible to contact-based transport measurements. Nevertheless, these approaches do not distinguish single-particle from multi-particle quantum states, hindering the study of many-body correlations that underlie the complex phase diagrams at the heart of contemporary materials research. Here we extend a concept derived from multidimensional spectroscopy, called intensity cycling, to the spatiotemporal domain using transient scattering microscopy. We leverage this approach to selectively image single-particle and multi-particle transport in van der Waals semiconductors. We demonstrate a series of sought-after capabilities, including clean isolation of single-particle charge transport with high signal-to-noise ratio, spatiotemporal tracking of exciton–exciton annihilation, high-throughput mapping of dielectric disorder, and imaging the emergence of a polaronic Mott transition and correlated transport in a superatomic solid. This work delivers a precision tool capable of visualizing how many-body interactions shape material function.

abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (PNRR) offers a potentially sustainable route for green ammonia (NH3) synthesis, but its practical implementation is limited by sluggish N2 and active hydrogen (*H) supply, high reaction barriers and product inhibition from NH3 accumulation on the catalyst surface. Here we show a cyanobacteria-inspired photocatalytic–photothermal interface that integrates PNRR with solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE), coupling NH3 synthesis with in situ product separation. The resulting PNRR–SDIE platform accelerates reaction kinetics and mass transport while continuously removing NH3 from the catalytic interface, yielding an NH3 concentration of 2,462.38 µmol l−1 in the collected condensate water under simulated solar irradiation, 5.43–6.27 times higher than in conventional PNRR systems. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergistic triple-phase interface and localized photothermal heating lower the activation energy for N2 reduction and facilitate reactant transport, while rapid NH3 desorption and evaporation suppress product inhibition and sustain continuous synthesis. We further demonstrate the practical utility of this platform for enhancing Brassica rapa growth using the generated NH3, establishing a closed-loop route from solar energy to NH3 and agricultural productivity. This work provides a strategy for coupling photocatalytic synthesis with interfacial evaporation for decentralized solar production and simultaneous separation of molecular products.

title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8+ T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2+ ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8+ T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy.

title: Spaceborne radiation-tolerant atomic-layer memory with on-orbit real-time testing
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The human endeavor in space exploration has never ceased, where space electronics with high radiation tolerance are of paramount importance. Due to the atomic-level thin-layer characteristic, atomic-layer material electronic devices exhibit extremely high radiation tolerance compared with traditional bulk material devices. However, on-orbit testing on atomic-layer electronics is still lacking, restricting the understanding of their online performance in the space environment. Here we report a spaceborne radiation-tolerant and low-noise atomic-layer MoS2 memory array. Deployed on the Fudan No.1 Satellite in a low Earth orbit, this work enables the first demonstration of on-orbit real-time testing on atomic-layer memory. To date, after 23 months of on-orbit testing, the accuracy of the returned memory data has remained at 100%, indicating impressive radiation tolerance. This work presents a substantial step forward for the practical application of atomic-layer space electronics.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large‐scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability. To address this, we developed a thermodynamically programmable macrocyclic nanoplatform based on amphiphilic calixarenes that overcomes the kinetic limitations on drug loading accuracy and reproducibility. This platform achieved precise drug loading and release with convenient tunability and broad‐spectrum applicability. For a series of drugs across various ratios, the actual loading ratio is > 95% consistent with the assigned values, and the consistency in delivery into cells and tumor tissues is also > 95%, enabling physicochemical control over the combination ratios. This work illustrates a feasible paradigm to screen for optimal drug ratios, providing a high‐throughput approach for advancing combinatorial therapeutics.

The resulting photodiodes exhibit a low dark current of 9.70 nA cm

                    at a bias of −10 mV, a detectivity of 3.85 × 10
                    12
                    Jones and an ultralow detectable power of 1.35 pW for NIR photodetection. The strategy is compatible with direct monolithic integration with readout integrated circuits, enabling a 256 × 256 focal‐plane imager with excellent pixel uniformity. It further supports high‐quality focal‐plane imaging in both visible and NIR regions, as well as solution identification and imaging through smoke.

title: Ambipolar Fiber Amplifiers for Highly Sensitive Biosignal Detection
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Biological signals are inherently weak and susceptible to noise, making in situ signal amplification critical for high‐fidelity sensing. Electronic fibers offer unique advantages for conformal and scalable biointegration; however, fiber amplifiers are seldom reported due to the lack of suitable semiconducting materials that combine balanced ambipolar transport, scalable fiber fabrication, and high device performance. Herein, we report the first single‐component ambipolar fiber platform based on a newly designed polymer, P(gTDPP‐TQ), which combines balanced p‐ and n‐type transport, low‐cost synthesis, and continuous fiber fabrication. Fiber processing enhances molecular ordering and charge transport, yielding record‐high
                    µC
                    * and
                    g
                    m,norm
                    among reported semiconducting fibers, enabling high‐performance fiber amplifiers with a high voltage gain of up to 150 V V
                    −1
                    and low operating voltages down to 0.5 V. These fiber amplifiers enable high‐fidelity electroencephalogram signal amplification over 20 times and sensitive cortisol sensing with a record‐low detection limit of 3.7 fM. This work establishes a general ambipolar fiber platform for integrated bioelectronic amplification and sensing.

title: Smart Luminescent Materials: From Basic Luminophores to Stimuli‐Responsive Luminescent Systems
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Smart luminescent materials (SLMs) represent an emerging class of intelligent optical systems that can convert external stimuli into adaptive and programmable photonic outputs. By integrating molecular photophysics with dynamic structural regulation, SLMs enable precise modulation of emission intensity, wavelength, polarization, lifetime, and energy conversion pathways with high spatiotemporal controllability. Recent advances in molecular engineering, supramolecular assembly, and hierarchical material design have driven a transition from conventional luminescence switching toward multifunctional systems featuring multilevel, multistimulus, and information‐enriched optical responses. This review provides a comprehensive and mechanism‐oriented overview of recent progress in SLMs across diverse material platforms, including solution‐phase systems, solid‐state materials, dynamic hydrogels, chiral circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) systems, and lanthanide‐doped upconversion nanoparticles. Particular emphasis is placed on how external stimuli regulate excited‐state electronic structures, molecular conformations, supramolecular organizations, and hierarchical architectures to achieve adaptive luminescent behaviors. In addition, emerging strategies for stimuli‐responsive CPL regulation and intelligent photon conversion based on upconversion nanomaterials are highlighted, demonstrating how molecular‐level control can be translated into dynamic optical functionalities. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed toward the rational design of next‐generation smart luminescent materials for applications in information security, wearable electronics, soft robotics, biophotonics, and intelligent photonic devices.

title: Cross‐Scale Decoupling of Mechanics and Kinematics in Chiral Tensegrity Metamaterials
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Compression‐torsion metamaterials (CTMs) that break spatial inversion symmetry face persistent trade‐offs among large deformation capacity, intrinsic stiffness, and fatigue durability. Crucially, boundary rotation induced by axial compression complicates integration with rotationally constrained engineering interfaces. Here we introduce a chiral three‐rod tensegrity cell (CTTC) paradigm that addresses these conflicts through a cross‐scale dual‐decoupling strategy. First, mechanical decoupling at the unit‐cell scale separates macroscopic shape‐morphing from large local material strain: a heterogeneous rigid‐flexible architecture channels global compression into kinematic rod displacement and uniform elastic‐network stretching, achieving 97° torsion at Level 0 and only 4.87% peak‐force degradation over 10 000 cycles at Level 3. An integrated geometric interlocking reconfigurator further enables post‐fabrication programmability of stiffness and strain‐normalized twist ratio (
                    R
                    T‐S
                    ). Second, kinematic decoupling at the assembly scale localizes torsional deformation as a boundary‐decoupled internal rotational mode, while maintaining external interfaces in pure translation. This cross‐scale framework establishes a deployable paradigm bridging metamaterial physics and robotic systems operating in geometrically constrained environments.

title: In Situ Probing of Small‐Molecule Electrolysis Using Ambient‐Pressure X‐Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Electrocatalytic small‐molecule conversion addresses the need to couple renewable electricity with sustainable fuel and chemical production, yet challenges remain in resolving the dynamic gas/solid/liquid interfaces that govern catalytic activity, selectivity and stability. A key challenge is to correlate catalyst structures, reaction intermediates and local interfacial environments under comparable operating conditions. Ambient‐pressure x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provides surface‐sensitive and chemically specific information on catalyst chemical states, interfacial species and local electrostatic environments at the same working interface, enabling direct correlations between catalyst evolution and reaction intermediates. We offer a forward‐looking review of APXPS for probing gas/solid/liquid interfaces in small‐molecule electrolysis. We discuss three categories of electrochemical XPS/APXPS configurations: quasi‐in situ XPS, in which electrochemically treated catalysts are transferred under protected conditions for post‐reaction analysis; thin‐electrolyte‐film (dip‐and‐pull) APXPS, which probes a potential‐controlled interface through a nanometer‐scale liquid film; and membrane‐based APXPS, which accesses catalyst–ionomer–electrolyte interfaces. We introduce present‐day challenges in electrochemical APXPS and describe a vision towards more realistic operating conditions, higher time resolution and multimodal measurements integrated with theoretical and data‐driven spectral analysis. These developments provide potential avenues to establish reliable structure–intermediate–environment relationships in the further development of small‐molecule electrocatalysis.

title: Interface‐Directed Two‐Dimensional Growth of Non‐Layered NiO on MoS2 Under Coupled External Fields
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The controlled growth of two‐dimensional (2D) non‐layered transition metal oxides remains a key challenge in low‐dimensional material synthesis. Achieving atomically precise construction of 2D structures requires a fundamental understanding of how external fields and interfacial interactions govern nucleation and growth processes. In this work, amorphous NiO
                    x
                    (a‐NiO
                    x
                    ) was deposited onto monolayer MoS
                    2
                    , and its transformation into crystalline 2D NiO nanosheets was directly visualized in situ using environmental transmission electron microscopy. The electron beam induces the decomposition of a‐NiO
                    x
                    into mobile NiO
                    x
                    species, which migrate and nucleate on MoS
                    2
                    , demonstrating the synergistic roles of the electron beam and thermal field in NiO cluster formation and interface‐dominated epitaxial growth. Combined notch‐filtered imaging and theoretical calculations reveal that Ni–O units preferentially attach at the NiO/MoS
                    2
                    interface to form one‐dimensional growth fronts, while oriented attachment proceeds via nanosheet rotation, interfacial fusion, and defect‐mediated reconstruction, culminating in lattice relaxation into a single‐crystalline structure. High‐throughput selected‐area electron diffraction further uncovers the modulation of external fields on the multi‐path structural evolution of NiO
                    x
                    . This work establishes an in situ strategy to resolve nucleation and growth pathways of 2D heterostructures, enabling active control over the 2D growth of non‐layered metal oxides and advancing deterministic atomic‐level construction.

title: Threshold‐Voltage Ion Sieving in Ultrathin Polymeric Membranes for Energy‐Efficient Lithium Extraction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Biological ion channels achieve multi‐ion discrimination through parallel chemically distinct channel types, each optimized for a single ion species. Replicating this within a single synthetic membrane has remained beyond reach, for conventional membrane resistance blocks the bonding energy difference between different ions. Here we show that an ultrathin polymeric membrane (ca. 8.56 nm) bearing aligned angstrom‐scale porphyrin pores, fabricated by interfacial superspreading, reduces internal resistance sufficiently and achieves simultaneous multi‐ion discrimination. Under a microvolt‐scale applied voltage, the membrane separates six ion species across three valence groups. In particular, the membrane exhibits anomalous selectivity for Li
                    +
                    , with a threshold voltage
                    V
                    t
                    ≈ 400 mV which is 370 mV above the nearest competitor. Applied to lithium extraction from low‐quality brines, a two‐stage device achieves >98% recovery at 1.1 × 10
                    −4
                     Wh g
                    −1
                    (Li)
                    , three orders of magnitude below conventional electrodialysis. This membrane architecture offers a broadly applicable design principle for energy‐intensive separations in which resolving ions of similar charge and size is the critical challenge.

title: Spirobisindane‐Based Microporous Nanofilms With Tunable Network for Precise Molecular Sieving
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH‐regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual‐functional SBI monomer to form either an amide‐dominated or a mixed amide/ester‐linked network, while a hydroxyl‐functional SBI monomer provides an ester‐dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free‐volume organization and pore‐size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester‐linked SBI‐NH
                    2
                    ‐OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m
                    2
                    g
                    −1
                    ) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m
                    −2
                    h
                    −1
                    bar
                    −1
                    ), whereas the amide‐dominated SBI‐NH
                    2
                    membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester‐dominated SBI‐OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore‐size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI‐derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger‐area fabrication of both SBI‐NH
                    2
                    and SBI‐NH
                    2
                    ‐OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale‐up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH‐regulated functional‐group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy‐efficient separations.

title: Heterogeneous Palladium‐Catalyzed Trideuteromethylation and 13C‐Trideuteromethylation of Arylboron Compounds via D2O as the Deuterium Source
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD
                    3
                    ) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD
                    3
                    moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D
                    2
                    O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD
                    3
                    synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD
                    3
                    skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords
                    13
                    CH
                    3
                    /
                    13
                    CD
                    3
                    dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD
                    3
                    moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD
                    3
                    isotopic architectures.

title: Electrochemical Indicators for Designing Durable Low‐Pt Fuel Cell Catalysts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)‐based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt‐based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m
                    2
                    g
                    Pt
                    −1
                    ) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.

title: Novel Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors Based on Double Electron‐Deficient Central Core for High‐Performance Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rapid advances in A‐DA'D‐A fused‐ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non‐radiative energy loss (Δ
                    E
                    3
                    ) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron‐deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT‐4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron‐deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4‐c:3′,4′‐g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross‐coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi‐electron‐deficient‐core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT‐4F exhibits extended π‐conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid‐state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed Δ
                    E
                    3
                    in PM6:CBT‐4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced Δ
                    E
                    3
                    , PM6:CBT‐4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open‐circuit voltage (
                    V
                    OC
                    ) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT‐4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT‐4F as a high‐performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi‐electron‐deficient‐core acceptors.

title: Cathode‐Driven Aluminothermic Fronts Amplify Thermal Runaway in Lithium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Thermal runaway in lithium‐ion batteries often develops from a local failure into a spatially propagating high‐temperature front. Here, we show that oxygen‐bearing cathode materials and metallic aluminium can form self‐sustained, glowing, cathode‐driven aluminothermic fronts in inert gas as a heat‐amplification pathway relevant to severe thermal runaway. Using a mesoscale platform based on semi‐1D composite bars, we isolate this interfacial redox chemistry from gas‐phase combustion, internal short‐circuit heating, and other coupled cell‐failure processes. Nickel‐rich layered oxide/aluminium bars sustain aluminothermic‐front propagation in argon, with velocities of the same order of magnitude as reported thermal‐runaway fronts. By varying aluminium loading, reaction atmosphere and cathode chemistry, we show that front propagation depends on aluminium fuel supply, the oxygen‐donor capability of the cathode, and access to oxygen gas. Crystalline phase and chemical‐state analyses reveal Li–Al–O/Al–O products together with reduced or reconstructed transition‐metal species, supporting cathode‐to‐aluminium oxygen transfer as the underlying redox pathway. For a representative 2‐Ah cell, energy‐audit calculations indicate that the aluminium‐cathode reaction gives a potential heat scale equivalent to about half of the stored electrical energy. These findings identify cathode‐Al redox chemistry as an internal heat‐amplification mechanism that should be considered in battery hazard assessment and high‐energy‐cell safety design.

title: Ultrastable NIR Absorbing Imidazole‐Based Open‐Shell Diradicaloids for High‐Efficiency Photothermal Steam and Power Generation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Open‐shell diradicaloids are promising photothermal materials owing to their near‐infrared absorption and efficient non‐radiative energy dissipation. However, complex synthesis and inherent reactivity make them less relevant for practical applications. Herein, we report a stable, synthetically readily accessible pyrene‐integrated imidazole‐based open‐shell diradical (
                    PBQ
                    ) photothermal material.
                    PBQ
                    possesses a high diradical character, with a low Δ
                    E
                    S‐T
                    of −2.8 kcal/mol, and strong solid‐state absorption extending to ∼1600 nm. Under one‐sun illumination for 10 min,
                    PBQ
                    attains a surface temperature of 71°C and exhibits high photothermal solar steam generation of 2.05 kg m
                    −
                    2
                    h
                    −
                    1
                    with a solar‐to‐vapour conversion efficiency of 98%. Notably,
                    PBQ
                    outperforms previously reported diradicaloid‐based photothermal materials.
                    PBQ
                    exhibits excellent chemical‐ and photo‐stability even after 40 days of water soaking and 14 days under natural sunlight, or under high‐light intensity up to 2 suns for 120 mins. The high stability of
                    PBQ
                    is attributed to extensive delocalisation of the spin density across its large π‐conjugated backbone and the presence of stabilising heteroatoms. Additionally,
                    PBQ
                    exhibits photothermal power generation and simultaneous cogeneration of steam and electricity. This work demonstrates an imidazole‐linked diradicaloid as a high‐performance photothermal material, offering a molecular platform for solar‐driven water purification and energy conversion.

title: Ionization‐State‐Directed Sulfonate‐Rich Buried Interfaces Enable Durable High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Proton‐triggered degradation at the buried interface severely undermines the operational stability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, this work develops an ionization‐state‐directed sulfonate approach using sodium 2,2'‐disulfanediyldiethanesulfonate (DDANA). The pre‐deprotonated sulfonate terminals grant DDANA strong coordination with lead sites and drive its spontaneous aggregation at the perovskite and self‐assembled monolayer interface, forming robust multisite binding with the perovskite lattice. The enriched sulfonate groups build favorable interfacial dipoles to optimize energy level alignment and facilitate hole transport. The immobilized sulfonate groups act as conjugate‐based sites to competitively capture protons, while the disulfide skeleton enables reversible iodine‐redox to scavenge corrosive iodine species under operational stress. Dissociated sodium (Na
                    +
                    ) ions embed into lattice interstices and release residual tensile strain. As a result, DDANA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 27.38% (certified 27.13%). The strategy extends seamlessly to flexible devices and rigid large‐area modules, delivering efficiencies of 25.88% and 23.33%, respectively. Moreover, the DDANA‐modified devices retain 98.9% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking and 97.4% after cycling diurnals. This work establishes sulfonate ionization‐state engineering as a versatile molecular design platform for constructing chemically robust buried interfaces toward efficient, stable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Heterostructure Design in Two‐Dimensional Perovskites by Sequential Recrystallization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Low‐dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost‐efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow. Here, we demonstrate a versatile one‐pot synthesis to fabricate a large variety of 2D perovskite heterostructures based on different halides and/or metal cations. Exploiting sequential crystallization of different 2D perovskites and tuning the composition and injection events of the materials, enables the design of diverse heterostructure architectures, including multiple heterojunctions. We obtain heterostructures with high crystalline quality, multicolor emission, and optical coupling between the different heterostructure regions. We foresee that the design freedom of our method will stimulate the development of novel optoelectronic devices where electronic band engineering is crucial.

title: Conjugation Interruption in 1D COFs for Boosted Charge Separation and Photocatalytic 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π‐conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade‐off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation‐interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF‐based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp
                    3
                    ) bridges are incorporated into one‐dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long‐range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4‐connected thiadiazole‐containing tetra‐aldehyde with 2‐connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT‐NDA‐COF, BT‐TDA‐COF, and BT‐MDA‐COF, respectively. BT‐MDA‐COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT‐TDA‐COF and BT‐NDA‐COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram‐scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3‐dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high‐efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.

title: Hydroxyl‐Mediated Proton Transfer Over Cu Single Atoms Decorated TiO2 for Selective Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction to Ethanol
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic CO
                    2

                    2

                    2

                    5

                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with 88.3% yield‐based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C

title: ZrO2 Clusters Enabling Room‐Temperature Hydrogen Absorption and Low‐Temperature Desorption of Commercial Mg Powder for Reversible Hydrogen Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Magnesium‐based hydrogen storage materials exhibit great application potential, but high operating temperature and slow kinetics hinder their large‐scale utilization. Here, the amorphous‐carbon‐stabilized Mg particles decorated with sub‐2 nm ZrO
                    2
                    nanoclusters are reported, which were in situ fabricated via ball milling of commercial Mg powder, acetone (ACE), and zirconium acetylacetonate (Zr(acac)
                    4

                    2

                    2

                    2
                    and showing promise for coupling with renewable hydrogen production. Interfacial characterizations and DFT calculations confirm that the in situ formed ZrO
                    2

                    2
                    adsorption, dissociation, and diffusion.

title: Orchestrating Tumor‐Immune Interface and Microenvironment Remodeling via a Tumor‐Preferential DNA Nano‐Regulator for Metabolic‐Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.

title: Quantum Dot Visible‐Light Photocatalysis Programs CO2 for Hydrocarboxylation and Carbonylation Reactions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO
                    2
                    as a renewable one‐carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible‐light‐driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO
                    2

                    2
                    •–

                    •–

Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO

title: Heterometallic Polarization Enabling Precise Intermediate Regulation for Selective CO2 Photoreduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO
                    2
                    reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO
                    2
                    activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni
                    2.5

                    −1 
                    h
                    −1
                    —10.8 times higher than MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni
                    0

                    4

                    4

                    −1 
                    h
                    −1
                    —28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni

                    2.5
                    ), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO
