title: CD8+ T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of
                    Plasmodium falciparum
                    infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8
                    +
                    T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)–regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8
                    +
                    T cell–dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8
                    +
                    T cell–mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8
                    +
                    T cell–induced endothelial death in CM.

title: Strigolactone receptor D14 integrates phosphate and strigolactone signaling by interacting with and stabilizing PHR1
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Strigolactone (SL) and low phosphate (LP) signaling coordinately regulate shoot and root architecture and plant adaptation. While LP signaling is generally considered upstream of SL biosynthesis, their interaction is more complex. For instance, exogenous SL exerts opposite effects on lateral root formation under low versus high phosphorus. Here, we show that under LP, SL-induced anthocyanin accumulation requires PHR1, demonstrating that PHR1 functions downstream of SL signaling. We uncovered an SL-dependent physical interaction between PHR1 and the SL receptor DWARF14 (D14). This interaction promotes PHR1 dimerization, stabilizes PHR1 by inhibiting its ubiquitination-mediated degradation, and enhances its transcriptional activation activity. The D14-PHR1 complex directly binds and up-regulates the SL biosynthesis gene
                    MAX3
                    and anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, thereby inhibiting branching and hypocotyl elongation and promoting anthocyanin accumulation. These findings indicate that PHR1 mediates the coordination of SL and LP signaling, potentially explaining SL’s opposing effects on lateral root formation under different phosphorus conditions. In the
                    phr1
                    mutant, exogenous SL inhibited lateral roots under both LP and Pi-sufficient conditions, confirming that the promoting role of SL under LP requires PHR1. PHR1 also interacted with D14 to activate
                    LBDs
                    and
                    HB23
                    , regulating lateral root formation. Collectively, LP signaling coordinates with SL signaling via two parallel pathways: regulating SL biosynthesis to align SL functions with LP requirements and enhancing PHR1 activity through PHR1-D14 interaction to amplify LP signaling outputs.

title: Dual-acting compounds that deliver an acidifying domain via zanamivir to the virus surface are potent influenza inhibitors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: While contemporary antiviral development primarily strives to produce “lock and key” inhibitors, we present here a different approach to drug design that uses compounds devised to alter the microenvironment of the virion surface, making it incompatible with virus entry. We illustrate this strategy with inhibitors of influenza virus and show that compounds designed to produce a proton-rich mantle above the virion surface affect the ability of the viral hemagglutinin to interact with cellular receptors and gain entry to the cell. The compounds show exceptional antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo and protect against influenza illness in ferrets and in mice after a single dose, either therapeutically or prophylactically.

title: High-impulse and reactant-regenerative combustion-based micro actuators
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The use of combustibles in micro-actuator technologies enables powerful impulsive actuation capabilities comparable to those of natural organisms. However, the exogenous dependence of fuel limits the development of combustion-based actuators. We present a closed-cycle reactant regeneration strategy wherein the bidirectional interconversion between hydrogen and water achieves real-time fuel replenishment for reactant-regenerative electrolysis and combustion reactions. Based on this, we develop a 1.5-centimeter actuator that generates forces above 20 newtons and operates continuously for >7200 cycles without refueling (a two orders-of-magnitude improvement over existing combustion-based actuators). Experiments confirm its strength and cross-environment versatility for removing obstacles, jetting, and striking via underwater cavitation. These features enable the actuator to be integrated into small robotic platforms, allowing them to reconfigure local surroundings in an active manner.

title: Structure of the Chimalliviridae bacteriophage Goslar reveals host recognition and infection machinery
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Large-genome bacteriophages (phages) of the
                    Chimalliviridae
                    family have a distinctive life cycle, building compartments inside infected bacterial cells that broadly protect their genomes from host defenses. Here, we use cryo–electron microscopy to determine a structure of the
                    Escherichia coli
                    –infecting
                    Chimalliviridae
                    phage Goslar. We combine manual modeling of 25 structural proteins with AlphaFold structure predictions of an additional three proteins to generate a composite model with 2888 protein chains from 28 different structural proteins, totaling more than 1.4 million amino acid residues. Our structure reveals the architecture of the Goslar capsid, portal, tail, and baseplate, highlighting structural similarities and differences with other tailed phages. Combining our structural data with quantitative mass spectrometry of Goslar virions, we identify several high-copy virion-associated proteins that likely play key roles when injected into host cells upon infection. We also identify a
                    Chimalliviridae
                    -specific family of proteins that form long, flexible filaments anchored at the phage baseplate and which incorporate carbohydrate-binding domains, suggesting a key role in host recognition.

title: Quantum-interference metrology of dissipative Kerr solitons
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Dissipative Kerr solitons in optical microresonators underpin chip-scale frequency combs with applications ranging from coherent telecommunications to precision spectroscopy. Yet the characterization of their intrinsic femtosecond temporal structure remains challenging, as the low pulse energy and broad spectral bandwidth necessitate optical amplification and careful dispersion compensation in conventional ultrafast diagnostics, both of which can substantial distort the waveform. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-interference metrology of microcomb solitons based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. By attenuating the soliton stream to the single-photon level and measuring fourth-order interference, we directly retrieve near transform-limited pulse durations without amplification or dispersion management, remaining accurate even after propagation through 25 kilometers of standard fiber. The same interferogram also provides direct access to the temporal separations in multisoliton states by converting intersoliton separations into additional interference dips at corresponding delays, enabling subpicosecond characterization of their intracavity temporal structure. This quantum-inspired paradigm introduces a metrological approach that is immune to amplification and dispersion distortions, offering a powerful tool for the characterization of complex soliton physics.

title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The most extreme heat waves are intensifying faster than moderate events across many mid-latitude regions. Climate models underestimate these trends, suggesting an incomplete representation and understanding of the underlying physical processes. Here, we use an explainable machine-learning framework to investigate interactions among atmospheric circulation, surface soil moisture, and temperature, and their role in recent heat extremes. We show that a three-way interaction among these components becomes active once a critical temperature threshold is exceeded, contributing, on average, ∼10% to peak temperature anomalies during the most extreme heat events across ∼28% of humid mid-latitude regions. We further reveal that this interaction is systematically underestimated in CMIP6 and CESM2 Large Ensemble simulations. Soils in climate models are too dry at the initiation of heat waves, therefore suppressing subsequent soil-moisture depletion and inhibiting feedback activation. These findings help explain regional model biases in upper-tail warming and highlight avenues for improving future projections of extreme heat events.

title: Photonic entanglement swapping with remote quantum dots
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Entanglement swapping is a protocol that details how to create entanglement between previously uncorrelated particles. Its photonic version, mediated by the interference of photon pairs generated by separate quantum systems, finds disparate applications in quantum networks. So far, entanglement swapping with entangled photons from remote systems has been implemented only using probabilistic sources. However, the scaling up of quantum networks requires nonprobabilistic quantum emitters without a trade-off between the degree of entanglement and photon-pair generation rate. Here, we demonstrate photonic entanglement swapping using photon pairs generated by two separate GaAs quantum dots. The emitters are deterministically embedded in hybrid semiconductor-piezoelectric devices that make the entangled photons from two dissimilar quantum dots nearly identical. Entanglement swapping is demonstrated with a fidelity as high as 0.71(2), more than 10 SDs above the classical limit. The experimental data are quantitatively explained by a theoretical model that also suggests how to boost the protocol performance. Our work opens the path to the exploitation of quantum dot entangled-photon sources in quantum repeater networks.

title: A full-hardware edge detection system based on a highly robust dual random number generator
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO
                    
                      x
                    
                    /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we designed a low-power edge detection unit using dual random number hardware computation. Its energy consumption is 92.3% lower than traditional logic circuits, with strong anti-interference. To validate practical use, we constructed a 32-channel parallel full-hardware system with 64 devices, achieving 31.25 frames per second and excellent edge detection. The system exhibits excellent scalability, stability, and anti-interference, offering great potential for edge vision hardware in autonomous driving, safety monitoring, and surgical assistance.

title: Measuring mixed-state topological invariant in open photonic quantum walk
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Pure-state manifestations of geometric phase are well established and have found applications across essentially all branches of physics, yet their generalization to mixed-state regimes remains largely unexplored experimentally. The Uhlmann geometric phase offers a natural extension of pure-state paradigms and can exhibit a topological character. However, observation of this invariant is impeded by the incompatibility between Uhlmann parallel transport and Hamiltonian dynamics, as well as the difficulty of preparing topologically nontrivial mixed states. To address this challenge, we report an experimentally accessible protocol for directly measuring the mixed-state topological invariant. By engineering controlled nonunitary dynamics in a photonic quantum walk, we prepare topologically nontrivial mixed states from a trivial initial state. Then, by machine learning the full density matrix in momentum space, we directly extract the quantized geometric phase of the nontrivial mixed states. Furthermore, we observe that this transition of the quantized mixed-state topological invariant from a trivial to a nontrivial value is closely associated with the emergence of a topological kink structure. These results highlight a geometric phase framework that naturally extends to open quantum systems both in and out of thermal equilibrium.

title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage.
                    TERT
                    promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

title: MYC primes a paralog synthetic lethality involving the mitochondrial translocase subunits TIMM17A and TIMM17B and N-Acetylaspartate
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
To identify the genes and pathways required for the survival of
                    MYC
                    -amplified cancers, we engineered an isogenic cell system in which transformation is driven by oncogenic
                    MYC
                    . Using a genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 library, we identified the mitochondrial membrane translocase TIMM17A as uniquely essential for the survival of MYC-transformed cells. This dependency arises from MYC-driven suppression of
                    TIMM17B
                    , the paralog of
                    TIMM17A
                    . TIMM17A/B is an essential component of the TIM23 mitochondrial protein import complex, and the MYC-induced suppression of
                    TIMM17B
                    creates a strong dependency on
                    TIMM17A
                    . N-acetylaspartate supplementation rescued
                    TIMM17A
                    dependency in
                    MYC
                    -amplified cell lines, highlighting the unique and crucial role of this metabolite in the cell fitness of
                    MYC
                    -amplified cancers. These observations identify a paralog dependency required for the survival of a subset of MYC-driven cancers.

title: Intuitive knowledge of object acoustics enables perceptual separation of physical variables from impact sounds
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Upon hearing objects collide, humans can estimate physical attributes such as material and mass. Although the physics of sound generation is well established, the inverse problem that listeners solve—of inferring physical parameters from sound—remains poorly understood. Classical accounts posit the use of acoustic cues that correlate with physical variables but do not explain how humans might distinguish multiple concurrent physical causes. To study this problem, we measured impulse responses from hundreds of everyday objects, extracted their resonances, and used statistics of the resonances to build a probabilistic generative model of impact sounds. We then used the model to synthesize and manipulate stimuli for experiments measuring judgments of physical variables. Humans accurately judged object properties from collision sounds. However, when both of the colliding objects varied, performance was impaired if the distribution of object resonances deviated from those measured in real-world objects. The results suggest that humans have internalized the statistical regularities of real-world object acoustics, and use this knowledge to separate the acoustic contributions of the distinct objects in the world that give rise to sounds.
